narrator.instruct: Fast, gripping, high-energy history storyteller. Excited and urgent, amazed, punchy emphasis on the shocking moments, brisk pace, no long pauses.

boatman.instruct: A terrified old river boatman shouting over roaring water, panicked and amazed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Mississippi River once flowed backward.

voice.instruct: Dramatic, amazed opening hook, urgent, hitting 'backward' hard.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In eighteen eleven and eighteen twelve, giant earthquakes shook New Madrid, Missouri.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Riverbanks cracked and crashed into the water.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the land under the river pushed up, like a giant step.

lines.speaker: boatman
lines.text: The river's running the wrong way!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: For a few hours, part of the current rushed upstream. Waterfalls roared across the river.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Boat crews fought huge waves, and whole trees fell into the river.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the water turned south again. But the land was changed forever.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The sunken ground even filled up into a brand new lake, Reelfoot Lake.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: For a moment, the mighty Mississippi ran the wrong way.
